issues.legal_issue: Reliable evidence of cruel treatment and the surrounding circumstances can support convictions for causing a death with common intention despite a defence that the fatal injuries were accidental or that the deceased was mentally ill.
material_facts: Medical evidence, which was almost unchallenged, established that the deceased died from burn injuries.
Neighbour witnesses gave evidence of cruel treatment; the court found no sufficient reason to reject their testimony.
The defence suggested that the deceased’s mental illness or an accident caused the burns, but the courts rejected that account, and the medical evidence ruled out one suggested accidental cause.
The appellants did not obtain medical treatment for the deceased or inform her parents of the burns before her death, and one appellant gave a false explanation for their cause.
issues.conclusion: The convictions of the two appellants found to have participated in the cruel treatment, for murder with common intention, were upheld.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied Section 302 read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code and upheld the convictions on the evidence accepted by the courts below. It cited no earlier cases.

rule.if: criminal_appeal_against_conviction and reliable_neighbor_evidence and deceased_suffered_cruel_treatment and death_from_burn_injuries and (failure_to_obtain_treatment or delayed_notice_to_family or false_explanation_for_injuries)

predicates.criminal_appeal_against_conviction: The matter is an appeal against a criminal conviction.
predicates.reliable_neighbor_evidence: Neighbours gave testimony about the deceased’s treatment, and the court found their testimony reliable.
predicates.deceased_suffered_cruel_treatment: The deceased was subjected to cruel treatment by people in her household.
predicates.death_from_burn_injuries: The deceased died from burn injuries.
predicates.failure_to_obtain_treatment: Those responsible for the deceased did not obtain medical treatment for her injuries.
predicates.delayed_notice_to_family: The deceased’s family was not told of her injuries before she died.
predicates.false_explanation_for_injuries: An accused gave a false explanation for how the deceased received her injuries.

issues.definition: When a criminal appeal challenges a conviction and reliable evidence of cruel treatment, fatal burn injuries, and post-injury conduct supports the prosecution account, the shared murder conviction is upheld.

issues.legal_issue: A shared murder conviction cannot stand against an accused where the evidence does not specifically implicate that accused and there is no other evidence against them.
material_facts: The witnesses who spoke of cruel treatment did not specifically state that this accused had treated the deceased cruelly.
The Court found no other evidence against this accused.
The evidence supporting the convictions of the other appellants did not establish this accused’s participation.
issues.conclusion: The accused’s conviction and sentence for murder with common intention were set aside.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied Section 302 read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code but found the evidence insufficient to sustain this accused’s conviction. It cited no earlier cases.

predicates.criminal_appeal_against_conviction: The matter is an appeal against a criminal conviction.
predicates.no_specific_evidence_of_accuseds_partici: The evidence does not specifically identify the accused as having participated in the relevant conduct.
predicates.no_other_evidence_against_accused: There is no other evidence implicating the accused.

issues.definition: When an accused appeals a conviction and neither specific evidence nor other evidence implicates them, the shared murder conviction is set aside.

issues.legal_issue: A conviction for causing the disappearance of evidence or concealing an offence may be upheld where the appellate court finds the conviction proper and the surrounding post-offence conduct includes a false account and failure to disclose the injury.
material_facts: One appellant was convicted under Section 201 of the Indian Penal Code.
That appellant gave a false explanation for the cause of the deceased’s burn injuries.
The deceased was not taken for medical treatment and her parents were not informed of the injuries before her death.
The Court held that the conviction under Section 201 was proper and legal.
issues.conclusion: The conviction under Section 201 was upheld.
issues.legal_principle: The Court upheld the conviction under Section 201 of the Indian Penal Code on the circumstances it accepted; it cited no earlier cases and did not set out a separate test for applying that provision.
